archival_memory.archie_age: Archie is three years old now.
archival_memory.archie_puppy: I vividly remember how he'd tumble over himself trying to figure out 'sit' and 'stay.' It's wild how big he's gotten now.
archival_memory.video_calls: I video call my parents almost daily, and Archie always seems to recognize my voice.
archival_memory.family_influence: My dad is a software engineer, and he's part of the reason I got into computer science in the first place. We used to do these small coding exercises together when I was in high school. He'd challenge me to figure out a puzzle or a problem, and it sparked that early fascination with logic and technology that eventually led me to major in CS. My mom, on the other hand, works as a nurse. She's the most caring person I know, and she's always the emotional backbone of our family. Even if it's late at night, she'll pick up my calls when I need a pep talk or if I'm worried about an upcoming exam. Between my parents, I found this healthy balance: I got the analytical edge from my dad and the empathetic side from my mom. My sister, well, she's just a ball of energy—constantly on social media, playing new games, or looking for the next big trend. She's so plugged into technology that sometimes she jokes she's going to overshadow me in the tech scene. She might be right.
archival_memory.family_traditions: One of our family traditions is going on a Saturday morning hike whenever I'm in town. We pack some snacks, load Archie into our SUV, and drive out to this trail about twenty minutes away. The path isn't super long, but it has a great view at the summit of a small bluff that overlooks a lake. Archie loves it—he's got endless energy. By the time we're at the top, he's chasing squirrels and sniffing every tree. Watching him run around like that reminds me to appreciate the small things. I can get so wrapped up in code and classes that I forget to just breathe and enjoy nature.
archival_memory.grandma_teasing: My grandma still teases me about the time I broke her antique vase when I was in middle school by throwing a mini football around her living room. I try to tune out that story, even though it's retold almost every Thanksgiving.
archival_memory.family_holidays: Holiday gatherings are a big deal in my family. Thanksgiving is practically a potluck extravaganza, with all kinds of dishes that make you want to hibernate until Christmas. Archie, of course, tries to snag anything that drops on the floor. We learned the hard way he has a sensitive stomach—one year he got into some leftover turkey bones, and we had to make a late-night veterinary visit. Ever since then, we're super careful about what 'people food' he can get his paws on.
archival_memory.family_influence_on_career: I find it interesting how family shapes who you become. Even though I'm on my own at college, I realize that a lot of the patience and resilience I rely on while working through tough programming projects actually comes from my parents. My dad taught me how to stay calm and break down problems, while my mom showed me how to be patient and empathetic—even when the situation is frustrating, like when a project partner doesn't pull their weight or code isn't cooperating. Plus, I can't forget my sister, who always pushes me to stay up on new trends so I don't become a relic in my twenties. Sometimes I do write about personal stories, like Archie or silly moments with my sister, in my personal statements for scholarships or grad school applications, because they matter to me that much.
archival_memory.family_description: We're supportive, close-knit, and lively. The way they come together around Archie, fussing over him or laughing at his antics, shows me what unconditional love looks like. I may be a busy fourth-year with internship interviews, clubs, research, and everything else on my plate, but at the end of the day, it's nice to know there's a place—and a family—where I'm always welcome, dog hair and all. I think that's what keeps me going, to be honest. No matter how many lines of code fail to compile, I can always count on home to recharge me. And yes, that definitely includes Archie leaping into my arms the second I walk through the door.
archival_memory.friendship_importance: my closest friends have become my second family at college
archival_memory.roommate_best_friend: Tony, my roommate and best friend from freshman year
archival_memory.sailing_club_friends: I met some great friends through the campus sailing club. It's a unique mix of personalities, and we all share a love for problem-solving. The camaraderie on the boat is special, and we rely on each other to stay motivated. One friend, Mariah, has been a close confidante and encouraged me to apply for a research position in data science.
archival_memory.computer_science_connections: I've made many connections through my computer science classes, including study groups, group projects, and late-night coding sessions in the lab. One particularly memorable experience was bonding with Carla over pizza at 3 a.m. during a difficult systems programming course. We were the only two left in the lab that late, and our shared struggles with memory management bugs created a strong bond between us.
archival_memory.gym_friends: I have some great friends from the gym. We started as a friendly circle of people who would work out together in the early mornings. One of my closest friends, Dean, is a fellow computer science major who's into machine learning and hardware acceleration projects. We bonded over our shared interests and now we share nutritional tips, workout regimens, and even game together. It's a friendship built around mutual support and pushing each other to be better in multiple areas of life.
archival_memory.gaming_friends: I have a circle of friends from the gaming club. We meet in a common lounge in the student center and play multiplayer strategy games. It's a great way to relax and have fun with friends. I made a great friend, Derek, through the club. He's super skilled in networking security and taught me some useful techniques for a cybersecurity research project. Our friendship evolved naturally from a shared hobby and later we supported each other academically.
archival_memory.library_friends: I have a friend, Jackson, whom I met in the campus library. We started chatting during water breaks, comparing our respective workloads. We discovered that we shared an interest in debates, particularly about the intersection of technology and society's legal structures. Our friendship is more intellectual than some of my others, but it's one I truly value because it broadens my perspective beyond code and servers.
archival_memory.everyday_life_friends: I've made great friends in unexpected, everyday-life situations, like in the dorm laundry room or while waiting in line for coffee. One day, I was stressed with a research deadline and was waiting in a long line for coffee. I started complaining about needing more time for my research code to run, and the person behind me heard me. It turned out she was also going through a tough time with her mechanical engineering lab project. We commiserated, shared a laugh, and ended up sitting together for coffee. We bonded over academic stress and exchanged contact info. Now, whenever we see each other on campus, we make a point to catch up. It's a positive, supportive relationship that started organically.
archival_memory.friendship_unifying_factor: Mutual respect and the sense that we're all navigating this crazy journey together. The high workload and pressure can create deep connections among computer science majors. We form bonds through critiquing each other's code, collaborating on projects, and supporting each other through late-night coding sessions.
archival_memory.graduation_dread: I'm excited about the future, but I'm also dreading the day when all my friends scatter to different corners of the world. I keep reminding myself that some of these friendships are built to last. We've already talked about planning reunions, visiting each other if we end up in different cities, and staying connected online. It's weird thinking how we'll be grown adults in different jobs, possibly different time zones, but hopefully still able to maintain the bond we forged here.
archival_memory.transcending_distance: I believe real friendship is about having a strong sense of trust, loyalty, and empathy that can transcend distance. I've seen this in my friends, like Tony, who's interning across the country, yet we still FaceTime regularly. I also see it in Carla, who's applying to master's programs abroad. We've promised to visit each other if either of us ends up in Europe. It's amazing how friendships can endure despite physical distance.
archival_memory.gratitude_for_friends: I'm extremely grateful for the friendships I've made through sailing, the gym, gaming, research, and random campus encounters. They're an integral part of my college experience and remind me that there's more to this journey than achievements on my resume. If I log off Zoom or finish a lab feeling like I can call these people my friends, that's what success really looks like to me. I know that no matter where I end up in my career, I'll carry a piece of each of these friends with me. Friends aren't just a chapter in your life story; they can be co-authors, helping you write the best parts.
